package_info.why_malicious: The website was compromised by attackers who injected a malicious JavaScript skimmer. This script exfiltrates payment card and private data entered by customers during checkout to attacker-controlled domains, constituting a classic Magecart attack.

execution_context.file_location: Injected inline in HTML or as an external script reference (e.g., in <script> tag on payment page)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code loads an external JavaScript skimmer from a Base64-encoded URL, which then executes in the context of the checkout page, intercepts payment form data, and exfiltrates it to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading an external script from a Base64-encoded URL is a common obfuscation technique used to evade detection. The loaded script is not part of the legitimate website and is fetched from a suspicious domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce sites should only load scripts from trusted, first-party or well-known third-party sources. Obfuscated or encoded script sources are not expected.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Base64-encoded script URLs are rarely, if ever, used legitimately in production e-commerce environments.
key_indicators: Script loaded from a domain not associated with the business
Script injected into sensitive payment page

execution_context.file_location: External JavaScript loaded from attacker domain (e.g., google-standard[.]com/sk.js)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks the payment form submission event, collects all entered payment and personal data, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting form submissions and exfiltrating sensitive data to an untrusted external domain is a hallmark of web skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Payment forms should only submit data to the legitimate payment processor or backend, not to third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form data may be sent to analytics or payment processors, but only to trusted, documented endpoints.
key_indicators: Event listener on payment form submission

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to the website and injects a malicious script tag with a Base64-encoded external source.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious skimmer script is loaded into the checkout page.

attack_chain.action: The external skimmer script executes, hooks into the payment form, and collects user-entered payment data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collected data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The skimmer script sends the stolen payment and personal data to attacker-controlled domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credit card and personal information.

behavioral_signatures: Inline or external scripts loaded from non-standard, suspicious, or recently registered domains
JavaScript code that hooks form submission events and sends data to external domains
file_indicators: References to domains such as google-standard[.]com, bing-analytics[.]com, etc.
Unexpected script tags on payment or checkout pages
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains like google-standard[.]com, bing-analytics[.]com, google-money[.]com, etc.
Unusual traffic to recently registered or non-canonical domains during checkout
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for script tags in HTML that load resources from suspicious or encoded sources, especially on payment pages. Inspect JavaScript for event listeners on forms that send data to external domains. Use network monitoring to detect POST requests to known skimmer domains. Flag any new or unrecognized domains in script sources or network traffic, particularly those registered recently or not associated with the business.
